An adversarial review pass (gpt-5.6-sol, 2026-07-18, run alongside the 9.30.0 tables wave) rated this a **blocker** in the 9.29.0 rm→trash commit `ae212caf` — recorded here for the owner to adjudicate.

**Finding**: broad destructive targets were auto-rewritten to `trash` with no filesystem-root, home, or workspace-parent guard. Probes returned allow-rewrites for:

- `rm -rf --no-preserve-root /` → `/opt/fake/trash /`
- `rm -rf /Users/yasyf/Code` → `/usr/bin/trash /Users/yasyf/Code`

Both were **denied** before `ae212caf`. Trash is recoverable by design, but moving `~/Code` (every repo) or attempting `/` to the Trash is still deny-tier.

---

## RESOLVED — general pack 0.27.0 (rm-guard wave 2, 2026-07-18)

`blast_radius_block` (captain_hook/packs/general/deletions.py) adds three hard-deny tiers on the macOS rewrite path — the filesystem root (`== Path("/")`), a home directory (`Path.home()`, `/Users`, `/Users/<x>`), and any directory that `contains_repo` (a bounded, fail-closed 20k-entry scan for a `.git`/`.jj` child). Gated on `rewritable` so non-macOS / non-spliceable paths keep byte-identical behavior at zero scan cost. Tier order is equality-before-scan; paths are `os.path.normpath`-normalized first so a trailing `..` can't dodge the equality tiers. Live-verified: `rm -rf --no-preserve-root /` → "filesystem root" deny; `rm -rf ~/Code` → "contains git/jj repositories" deny.

The same wave also closed the `bash -c 'rm -rf /'` bypass (check-only descent into `sh`/`bash -c` payloads and `eval`, combined `-…c` clusters included) and fixed cwd-threading on a failed/piped `cd`. Full decision record: [[rm-trash-rewrite-shipped]] / note ff6bcdbf; threat model doc 54548bc9. Reviewed by a codex sol finder + Claude opus refuter; the surviving gaps (subshell-`cd`, wrapper option-arity, case-insensitive APFS aliases) are deferred to backlog with a note, being adversarial-shaped rather than accident-shaped.
